answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Mine Toss first, then Spirited Away, then Bag of Tricks choosing its 3-Spark option against Nibbit, and finally Firework Finale against Nibbit. This uses all 3 energy, pays for both Spark-costed cards by using the Spark gained from the placed Bombs, deals 38 total damage, and gains 12 Block.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing Bag of Tricks’ 3-Spark option, Firework Finale, Spirited Away, and Duck and Cover instead of Mine Toss. That line would deal 33 damage and gain 17 Block, trading 5 damage for 5 extra Block.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the extra 5 Block from Duck and Cover. Since Nibbit’s telegraphed attack is exactly 12, that extra Block would not have changed survival this turn, so I prioritized the additional 5 damage from Mine Toss.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If Nibbit’s intent had been an attack for more than 12 damage, I would have preferred the higher-Block line with Spirited Away and Duck and Cover instead of Mine Toss, because the chosen line’s 12 Block would no longer fully cover the attack.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
